content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To join the army, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Complete the detailed security clearance questionnaire (4 hours)
Step 2. Attend the final enlistment ceremony (1 hour)
Step 3. Pass the physical fitness assessment (2 hours)
Step 4. Finalize the specific Military Occupational Specialty selection (2 hours)
Step 5. Undergo the initial background interview (1 hour)
Step 6. Receive the official duty station assignment (30 minutes)
Step 7. Complete the vision and hearing screening (1 hour)
Step 8. Review the service contract with a legal officer (2 hours)
Step 9. Submit proof of high school graduation or GED (15 minutes)
Step 10. Pack personal belongings for basic training (3 hours)
Step 11. Verify all medical records and immunization history (2 hours)
Step 12. Research various army career paths (5 hours)
Step 13. Obtain notarized parental consent if under age (1 hour)
Step 14. Schedule the departure date for boot camp (30 minutes)
Step 15. Attend a pre-shipment briefing (2 hours)
Step 16. Meet with a specialized career counselor (1.5 hours)
Step 17. Locate original birth certificate and social security card (2 hours)
Step 18. Visit the local recruiting office for the first time (1 hour)
Step 19. Take the oath of enlistment (30 minutes)
Step 20. Attend an Army career fair (4 hours)
Step 21. Complete a dental examination (1 hour)
Step 22. Receive a list of required items for training (20 minutes)
Step 23. Request official transcripts from previous schools (1 week)
Step 24. Fill out the preliminary interest form (20 minutes)
Step 25. Speak with a veteran about their experience (2 hours)
Step 26. Take the Armed Services Vocational Aptitude Battery (ASVAB) test (3 hours)
Step 27. Meet with a recruiter to discuss test scores (1 hour)
Step 28. Review the Army’s code of conduct (1 hour)
Step 29. Inform current employer of intent to enlist (15 minutes)
Step 30. Conduct a preliminary physical screening (45 minutes)
Step 31. Complete the full medical evaluation at MEPS (6 hours)
Step 32. Sign the housing and allowance paperwork (1 hour)
Step 33. Undergo a final drug screening (30 minutes)
Step 34. Discuss enlistment bonuses and incentives (1 hour)
Step 35. Complete the initial aptitude self-assessment (45 minutes)
Step 36. Provide references for the background check (1 hour)
Step 37. Watch an orientation video on Army life (1 hour)
Step 38. Select a primary and secondary job preference (1.5 hours)
Step 39. Begin a personalized pre-entry workout regimen (4 weeks)
Step 40. Consult with a recruiter regarding career benefits (2 hours)
Step 41. Apply for necessary security clearances (3 hours)
Step 42. Take the specialized language proficiency test (2 hours)
Step 43. Sign the initial enlistment agreement (45 minutes)
Step 44. Receive the official military ID card (30 minutes)
Step 45. Complete a character reference interview (1 hour)
Step 46. Undergo a fingerprinting session (30 minutes)
Step 47. Open a military bank account for direct deposit (1 hour)
Step 48. Review and sign the Statement of Understanding (30 minutes)
Step 49. Gather information on the GI Bill and education benefits (2 hours)
Step 50. Receive the official orders to report (15 minutes)
Step 51. Complete the vocational interest survey (1 hour)
Step 52. Say goodbye to family and friends (1 day)
Step 53. Confirm the availability of the chosen training slot (2 days)
Step 54. Participate in a "Future Soldier" training event (5 hours)
Step 55. Request letters of recommendation (2 weeks)
Step 56. Finalize the dependency and residency paperwork (2 hours)
Step 57. Perform a final document audit with the recruiter (2 hours)
Step 58. Take the cyber awareness challenge (1 hour)
Step 59. Submit the completed enlistment packet (1 hour)
Step 60. Confirm the basic training start date (15 minutes)
Step 61. Read the Army history and traditions handbook (3 hours)
Step 62. Attend a local community outreach meeting (2 hours)
Step 63. Obtain a certified copy of marriage or divorce decrees (3 days)
Step 64. Verify citizenship or residency status (1 hour)
Step 65. Meet with a financial counselor (1.5 hours)
Step 66. Watch a tutorial on military rank structure (1 hour)
Step 67. Purchase necessary toiletries for the first week (1 hour)
Step 68. Undergo a psychological evaluation (2 hours)
Step 69. Receive the initial medical clearance (1 hour)
Step 70. Browse the Army's official website for FAQ (2 hours)
Step 71. Complete the height and weight measurements (20 minutes)
Step 72. Review the Uniform Code of Military Justice (2 hours)
Step 73. Complete the credit history check (1 day)
Step 74. Prepare a list of questions for the recruiter (30 minutes)
Step 75. Discuss family support programs (1 hour)
Step 76. Update personal contact information (10 minutes)
Step 77. Validate the high school diploma with the board (2 days)
Step 78. Sign the life insurance and beneficiary forms (1 hour)
Step 79. Attend an informational seminar on military service (3 hours)
Step 80. Clear all outstanding civilian legal matters (1 week)
